subject.title: improve(gateway): tunable control-plane write rate limit, default unchanged

question: Should OpenClaw expose a gateway-wide knob that raises the shipped control-plane security limit for every identity, or require batching or an identity-scoped trusted-automation mechanism?
rationale: The choice changes an intentional security hardening and adds permanent config surface; code correctness alone cannot establish the desired trust and operational policy.

options.title: Keep the fixed limit
options.body: Use the existing JSON merge-patch path to batch rollout changes and avoid adding another security-sensitive config surface.

options.title: Design a scoped quota
options.body: Allow elevated throughput only for an explicitly authenticated automation identity, with focused security and isolation tests.

options.title: Accept the global knob
options.body: Sponsor the gateway-wide setting with explicit security ownership, audit guidance, and real burst/restart proof.

recommendation.title: Keep the fixed limit
recommendation.body: Use the existing JSON merge-patch path to batch rollout changes and avoid adding another security-sensitive config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and immediately hardened the current limiter and are the strongest history-backed owner for deciding whether its boundary may become configurable.
